title: Hazel and the Scholarship
premise: Theo Okafor, a senior raising his younger siblings while his mother works night shifts, sees the Meridian Prep scholarship as his only exit. When the application essay asks him to write about 'a truth that changed you,' he stumbles onto evidence that the school board buried a hazing death years ago to protect its donors—and that the scholarship fund itself was built on the cover-up. As Theo investigates, he risks losing the scholarship, his family's stability, and the friendship of the board chair's daughter, Hazel, who becomes his reluctant ally. In the end, Theo publishes the truth at the cost of the award, but the resulting scandal forces the district to reform the scholarship—and Hazel's testimony ensures he's offered it back on honest terms.
about_author: Isandro Oyelaran is a former public school teacher who spent six years in underfunded districts before turning to fiction full-time. He writes young adult stories about kids who carry adult weight, and lives with his sister's three cats, which he insists are co-authors.

chapters.title: Counting Days
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A morning routine montage: waking the twins, packing lunches, racing to Meridian Prep where he's the scholarship kid among the wealthy. He treats senior year like a prison sentence with graduation as release. Emotional beat: exhausted tenderness and quiet resentment toward a system that expects him to be both student and parent.

chapters.title: The Question
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. English class assigns the scholarship essay: 'Describe a truth that changed you.' Theo freezes—he has no safe answer. That night, cleaning out the school archive for his janitor shift-adjacent work-study, he finds a sealed 2009 incident report. Emotional beat: curiosity curdling into dread as the name on the report matches the library's memorial plaque.

chapters.title: What the Plaque Doesn't Say
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. He researches Daniel Reyes, the boy on the plaque who supposedly died off-campus. The incident report says otherwise: a hazing ritual at a donor's lake house, covered up by then-principal and current board chair Eleanor Voss. Emotional beat: the vertigo of realizing the institution feeding his family also buried a child.

chapters.title: Hazel
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Eleanor Voss's daughter notices Theo photographing board documents and confronts him—then covers for him when security arrives. Privileged and restless, Hazel has always sensed her mother's polished lies. Emotional beat: wary alliance; two people from opposite sides of the same secret recognizing each other.

chapters.title: The Price of Silence
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A guidance counselor hints that 'troublemakers' don't win scholarships. Then Theo's mom loses hours at her second job—a job at a Voss-owned property. The message is unmistakable. Emotional beat: fear and fury; Theo nearly burns the evidence to keep his family safe.

chapters.title: Reyes
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Theo and Hazel track down Daniel's older brother, now a long-haul driver, who confirms everything and begs them not to reopen the wound. But he slips them one thing: a letter Daniel mailed the week he died. Emotional beat: grief as living thing; the cost of truth measured in a survivor's scars.

chapters.title: Deadline
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Scholarship interviews approach just as Voss announces she'll chair the selection committee. Hazel discovers her mother plans to quietly dissolve the old scholarship fund—the paper trail—after this cycle. Emotional beat: the trap closing; Theo realizes exposing the truth and winning the award have become mutually exclusive.

chapters.title: The Essay
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Alone at 3 a.m., Theo finally writes the essay—not the safe sob story, but the whole truth of the cover-up, submitting it as his application. Hazel, meanwhile, copies her mother's private files. Emotional beat: catharsis and terror; the moment survival and integrity stop being the same goal.

chapters.title: Board Meeting
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the public board meeting, Theo reads his essay aloud; Hazel stands and corroborates with the files, defying her mother publicly. Voss unravels; the room turns. Emotional beat: the climax—courage as a public, irreversible act, and Hazel choosing truth over blood.

chapters.title: Graduation
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Weeks later: Voss resigns, an investigation opens, and the scholarship is restructured under independent oversight. Theo initially loses the award—then the new committee offers it back, and he accepts without shame. At graduation, his siblings cheer. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution; some prices aren't refunded, but some truths set you free anyway.
